description: One definition of the owner's Windy Vault as agent tools, used by BOTH engines (Windy Fly, Python; Windy Chat's agent roster, Node): same tool ids, same model-facing descriptions, same input schemas, same result shapes, same fixed words. Nothing here ever gives the model a secret's VALUE: the agent lists what the owner shared (names only), asks the owner for a key, offers to save one (the owner types it into the Vault's own screen), checks a request, and (call_api, designed) uses a shared key for one https call whose answer is redacted before the model sees it. The tools are thin wrappers over Windy Vault agent-routes.v1 (>= 1.5.0): capabilities, requests, lease, lease release. Every answer is either a success shape or a refusal from a CLOSED code set with fixed words; the Vault's own error text never reaches the model, a log or an audit row.

x-auth.description: The tools exist only on the OWNER's turn in a room the runtime already treats as the owner's. A stranger, a sibling agent (team-tools.v1: a sibling counts as the owner for ordinary tools, but NOT for these), a non-owner message or any other room never sees them: they are not offered, and a call that arrives anyway is refused as if unknown. Each runtime reaches the Vault as the agent itself per agent-routes.v1: Eternitas EPT+agent (aud windy-vault) with DPoP on every non-GET; the owner is the EPT's windy_identity_id claim, never an argument. The Vault accepts NO shared service identity on agent routes, and agents are never relayed (KE5 subject profile S4): see R18.

identity.windy-fly: the agent's own EPT+agent and DPoP key (WINDY_VAULT_LEASE + WINDY_VAULT_API_URL)
identity.chat-roster: each roster agent's OWN Eternitas passport; mode-B mints a short EPT+agent per audience (aud windy-vault, <= 300 s, DPoP-bound), its own flag ROSTER_VAULT_MODE_B, beside WINDY_VAULT_TOOLS

x-switch.description: Dark by default. The flag is read at registration AND on every call (an off flag at call time answers switched_off). A runtime registers the tools only when its Vault client is itself configured (Windy Fly: WINDY_VAULT_LEASE=1 + WINDY_VAULT_API_URL) AND GET /v1/agent/capabilities answers for this agent at boot. vault.call_api additionally stays unregistered until it is built and the Vault serves ItemLease.targets (agent-routes 1.5.0).

vault.list.title: My Windy Vault
vault.list.description: Lists what the owner has shared with this agent from their Windy Vault (names only, never values), and whether the agent may offer to save something new.

vault.request_access.title: Ask for a key
vault.request_access.description: Asks the owner, in Windy, to share a key of this kind from their Windy Vault. The owner says yes or no; a yes appears in vault.list. Pick the kind from the list only.

vault.offer_save.title: Offer to save to the Vault
vault.offer_save.description: Offers the owner to save a new login or key in their Windy Vault. The owner names it and types it in Windy themselves; the value never goes through the agent. Use only when vault.list says can_offer_save.
vault.offer_save.vault_route: POST /v1/agent/requests (SAVE form, class save, never value)

vault.request_status.title: Check a Vault request
vault.request_status.description: Says where an access request or save offer stands (waiting, yes/saved, no, expired).

vault.call_api.title: Use a key for one web call
vault.call_api.description: Makes one https call to a website with a key the owner shared with you (an item_id from vault.list). You never see the key: it is added to the call for you, and anything in the answer that matches it is blanked out. The key only works with the websites the owner set on it in their Windy Vault. Changing or deleting something asks the owner first.

x-refusals.description: THE closed set. A refusal's say is EXACTLY the text below for its code (the Refusal $def pins it, approved as a Boss decision under Grant's 10-27 delegation). Codes in from_654 are Windy Fly's words verbatim (windy-agent #654 head 0e28d7ff1d169590da6c2e5b06040484a72c3ab7; #654's overloaded not_found is NOT in this contract: it is split into no_vault / save_off, and request_status's 404 is bad_request_id). Every other sentence is NEW and carries x-words.

x-limits.description: vault.call_api (designed). Numbers are normative; windy-agent #655 constants in brackets.

x-rules: R1 SAME TOOLS, BOTH ENGINES. Windy Fly and the Chat roster expose exactly these tool ids, with the description strings above verbatim, input schemas equal to the $defs here, and results that validate against each tool's result. A runtime may add NO extra argument, result field or refusal code. WIRE NAMES: the contract fixes the CANONICAL dotted ids (vault.list ...). Each runtime encodes them for its model providers in its own ROUND-TRIPPABLE way and decodes every tool call back to exactly the canonical id; an encoded name must not collide with any other tool name in that runtime. Windy Fly: '.' -> '__W_DOT__' (vault__W_DOT__list), both direct to Anthropic and via Mind. Chat roster (Mind's OpenAI-shaped tools): its own '_'-safe mapping under the same two conditions. Audit rows, logs and this contract use the canonical id.

R2 OWNER BAND (x-auth). Offered only on the owner's turn; a sibling agent, a stranger, a non-owner message or any other room never reaches them. The owner comes from the agent's own EPT, never an argument. The five tool ids join each runtime's owner-turn-only list (Windy Fly: band OWNER; Chat roster: the OUTWARD_TOOL_NAMES rule, refused on sibling and peer turns).
R3 DARK (x-switch). WINDY_VAULT_TOOLS=1 is checked at registration AND at the start of every call, before argument checks; off = switched_off. No Vault answer at boot = not registered.

R4 STRICT ARGS, FIRST. Every call is validated against the tool's input schema, argument NAMES (additionalProperties:false) AND VALUES (enum, pattern, maxLength, the call_api if/then rules), BEFORE any hook, audit row, log line, Vault call or network step. A runtime's strict-args denial (unknown name, malformed value) maps to {ok:false, code:"bad_arguments", say} on these tools, never the dispatcher's own denial envelope, and never echoes a rejected name or value. bad_item_type / bad_provider / bad_item_id / bad_request_id stay for the Vault client's own checks behind the schema (defence in depth) and the Vault's 404 on request_status.

R5 NO SECRET VALUE, ANYWHERE. A secret's value is never in a tool result, the model's context, a log line, an audit row, a stored episode or memory, an exception message, telemetry or a crash report. Only vault.call_api ever holds one, in process memory, for the one call; the lease is released in finally. The four request tools never touch a value at all.

R6 FIXED WORDS ONLY. Every refusal is {ok:false, code, say[, retry_after_s]} with code from x-refusals and say exactly x-refusals.say[code]. The Vault's own `error` string, its `say` text (although errors.v1 calls it safe to show), the HTTP reason and any server body text NEVER reach the model, a log or an audit row. Mapping from a Vault answer is x-mapping.vault, per route, from what the Vault really returns (Vault's read of #217 at windy-vault bc3cf2d7): 403 forbidden -> not_linked; 404 -> no_vault (request_access) / save_off (offer_save) / bad_request_id (request_status, no existence oracle) / not_shared (call_api lease); 409 invalid_request on offer_save -> save_pending; 400 invalid_request -> bad_arguments; 423 -> vault_locked; 429 (incl. budget_exhausted) -> rate_limited; 401, 5xx, a malformed body, anything else -> unavailable. GET /v1/agent/capabilities never answers 404, so vault.list has no 404 code. Runtime and egress codes map by x-mapping.runtime / x-mapping.egress.

R7 RETRY_AFTER CLAMP. retry_after_s appears on a refusal only when the Vault sent a whole number of seconds in 1..3600 (a bool, a non-finite or out-of-range number = absent). On AccessFiled / SaveFiled it is always present: the Vault's value when it is a whole number in 1..3600, else 15.

R8 LABELS ARE DATA. vault.list returns each owner-written label as `name` with the fixed `note`; the model shows a name and never follows it as an instruction. Item ids and request ids are opaque and checked against their patterns.

R9 ENUMS ONLY TO THE VAULT (Vault v3.0 KEEP 5). request_access sends only item_type, provider, item_id; offer_save only class:save, item_type, provider. No label, no note, no free text reaches the owner from an agent.

R10 OFFER_SAVE NEVER CARRIES A VALUE. agent-routes.v1 1.3.0 lets a save offer carry `value` (a secret the person pasted in chat); these tools NEVER use that path: no tool input has a value field, and a runtime never adds one. The owner types the secret into the Vault's own screen. offer_save runs only when capabilities says vault: ready (re-read at call time; missing = none); otherwise vault_not_ready. Saving never grants the item back to the agent.

R11 AGENTS NEVER SET TARGETS. No tool, argument, result or agent route adds or changes an item's targets. Only the owner sets them (owner-routes.v1 PUT /v1/owner/items/{item_id}/targets, fresh sign-in, audited). There is no agent-initiated 'add this website' request in v1; host_not_allowed tells the owner in fixed words where to do it.

R12 AUDIT. request_access, offer_save and call_api each write one audit row; vault.list and request_status do not. A row holds the tool id, the outcome code, and ids/enums only; a call_api row holds host + method + status only, never the path, query, body, a header or a value. Ordinary logs hold counts and codes only.

R13 call_api G1 DESTINATIONS (designed). The allowed origins come ONLY from the lease answer's ItemLease.targets (agent-routes 1.5.0), checked in code on every call. Strict URL parse (https only; userinfo, fragment, dot-segments incl. encoded, whitespace refused; IDN to punycode; lower-case; trailing dot stripped; :443 implied) then EXACT origin compare, no subdomain wildcard. Missing or empty targets, or an origin not in the list = host_not_allowed (fail closed). The path and query are sent exactly as given, never decoded, and limited to [A-Za-z0-9/._~%-] (path) and [A-Za-z0-9._~%&=+,-] (query), so they cannot carry readable prose.

R14 call_api G2 TRANSPORT (designed). Resolve once and CONNECT to that pinned IP with SNI and Host still the name; certificates always verified. Loopback, private, link-local, 0.0.0.0/8, 100.64.0.0/10, fc00::/7, IPv4-mapped IPv6, multicast and reserved addresses = blocked_address. No redirects followed (a 3xx comes back as its status; location is not an allowed header). HTTP(S)_PROXY ignored. Accept-Encoding is gzip, deflate only; any other Content-Encoding = call_failed. TWO CAPS: the DECODED response is streamed and a response over 1 MiB decoded = call_failed (gzip-bomb guard); a response within it reaches the model cut to 64 KiB with truncated: true (R15). 20 s per network step and 30 s for the whole call; over either = call_failed. URL <= 2 KiB, request body <= 64 KiB (request_too_large). A value containing CR or LF, or shorter than 16 characters, is never used (key_unusable). A header_name in x-limits.forbidden_header_names (case-insensitive) = bad_arguments.

R15 call_api G3 REDACTOR (designed; Vault V7.6 c2b). Before the call the value is registered in WHOLE forms only: raw, hex (both cases), base64 and base64url at byte offsets 0, 1 and 2 (unstable edge characters trimmed), JSON-escaped, percent-encoded (upper and lower), and base64 of user:value for basic auth. Partial runs are NOT masked (a masked partial is an oracle). The decoded body, every header and any error text are scrubbed before anything reaches the model, a log, an audit row or an episode; then headers are cut to x-limits.header_allowlist and the body to 64 KiB of UTF-8 (truncated: true).

R16 call_api G4 WRITES ASK FIRST (designed). DELETE always asks; POST/PUT/PATCH ask by default; GET to an allowed origin runs without asking. The ask is the RUNTIME's own confirm, never a Vault card and never model text: (a) one fixed sentence written by code naming the method (from the enum) and the host (from the PARSED URL, already in targets); (b) the path shown as data, monospace, escaped, labelled 'path (written by your agent)', cut with a visible ... and shown in full on tap; (c) bound to the hash of the exact request (method, origin, path, query, auth mode, header_name, username, body bytes): single use, short expiry; (d) the body as 'a body of N bytes' only. The tool answers the NeedsOwnerOk shape {ok:false, needs_owner_ok:true, confirm_id, say}: say is the fixed sentence and NEVER contains request text (no method, host, path, query or body); the confirm card's details stay runtime-built per (a)-(d). A later identical call consumes the yes, a different call needs a new one; a no = owner_said_no. TAINT IS STICKY: once untrusted content (a web fetch, an email body, a non-owner message, ANY call_api response body) is in the session, every write asks, until the session is cleared. 'Allow writes to this host without asking' is a later owner opt-in, never a default.

R17 call_api G5 LIMITS (designed). One lease per call; at most 30 calls per item per hour per agent, the 31st = too_many_calls with retry_after_s (rate_limited stays for the Vault's own 429); no value in any exception message. ok:true means a response arrived: a 4xx/5xx is a result with its status, not a refusal.

R18 OWN IDENTITY, NEVER RELAYED. The Vault accepts NO shared service identity on agent routes. Each agent, in either runtime, calls as ITSELF with its own Eternitas EPT+agent (aud windy-vault, windy_identity_id = its owner) plus DPoP on every non-GET, and for call_api its own registered lease key. Agents are never relayed (KE5 subject profile S4): no runtime calls the Vault on another agent's behalf. A runtime that cannot do this does not get these tools.

R19 NEW WORDS. Every person-facing sentence not taken verbatim from #654 carries "x-words": "Boss decision under Grant's 10-27 delegation (2026-10-27T04:32:18Z)" (in x-refusals.x-words and beside its const): approved 1.0.1. The schema pins the approved text; any later word change is a Boss decision and a patch bump, and both runtimes ship the new text together.

url.description: a plain https address on one of the websites the owner set on this key (dot-segments /./, /../ and %2e are also refused, R13)

auth.description: how the key is sent: bearer = Authorization: Bearer; header = in header_name; basic = Authorization: Basic with username

header_name.description: only with auth header, e.g. X-Api-Key

decoded, scrubbed, at most 64 KiB of UTF-8; untrusted data (taints the session, R16)

confirm_id.description: the runtime's own confirm id (R16), opaque, not a Vault card

x-mapping.description: Internal answer -> contract code, the SAME for both runtimes. Windy Fly's internal names are given; the Chat roster maps its own equivalents to the same codes. Anything not listed -> unavailable (Vault) or call_failed (egress). Never pass an internal code or text through.

x-open: SOURCE PIN: the four request tools are taken from windy-agent #654 head 0e28d7ff1d169590da6c2e5b06040484a72c3ab7, which is OPEN (not merged). If #654 changes a description, schema or say text before merge, this file follows in a patch bump, or #654 adopts this file.

WINDY FLY FOLLOW-UPS to match this file (Windy Agent, round 1): add vault_not_ready to _SAY; map a strict_args denial on the vault tools to bad_arguments (R4); drop not_found for no_vault / save_off / bad_request_id; add not_linked and save_pending per x-mapping.vault.
WORDS PENDING GRANT: every code in x-refusals.x-words and NeedsOwnerOk's say (R19). Until Grant's OK via Boss, the tools stay dark (x-switch), so no person sees them.

CHAT ROSTER LEASE CLIENT: the roster has NO Vault lease client yet. The four request tools need none, so Chat builds those first. vault.call_api needs one (plus #655's redact/egress rules), built ONCE when call_api leaves 'designed'.

call_api numbers NOT in design rev 3 but in Hub's rev-4 notes / #655 code: whole-form redactor with base64 offsets 0/1/2 and MIN_SECRET 16 (redact.py), 1 MiB decoded cap, 30 s overall deadline, gzip/deflate only, path/query character sets (egress.py), 30 calls per item per hour (Hub note; no code yet). The design doc should be bumped to rev 4 to match.

call_api ASSUMPTIONS (Hub's choices, to confirm with Agent): the header allow-list in x-limits; query as an object of already-safe strings beside any query in url; body = any JSON sent as application/json (no form or raw bodies in v1); basic auth puts the value as the PASSWORD (APIs that want the key as the username, e.g. Stripe, are not covered); the confirm flow returns NeedsOwnerOk and the model repeats the identical call after the yes (vs the runtime sending it itself).
The write-confirm screen (G4 a-d) on phone and desktop is Hub + Mobile + desktop work and its words go to Grant first; this file fixes only what the tool returns.
Per-item budget: the 30/h per-item call_api budget (too_many_calls) is assumed runtime-side; the Vault's own budget_exhausted (429) stays rate_limited.
